turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Al Sade.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Nice to meet you.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: You're new with us, right? Can you tell me your full name and date of birth?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yeah, Kenji Watanabe. March 9th, 2011.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Thanks, Kenji. Is apparent with you today. My mom, Yumi.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: She's out in the car on a work call. She said I'm 15. I can handle it.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Fair enough. So what happened to the ankle?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: I rolled it at basketball on Sunday.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Wait, no, Saturday.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: It was Saturday morning practice. I went up for a rebound and came down on another guy's foot and it kind of turned in.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Ouch, which ankle?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Right one it swelled up right away. I limped off but I could walk.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Did you hear a pop or a snap?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No I don't think so.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: How bad is the pain now, zero to ten?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Like a six when I walk on it, maybe a two when I'm just sitting.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Any numbness or tingling in your foot? Nope.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: any pain in your knee or higher up the leg no just the ankle what have you done for it so far ice and I took two of the 200 milligram ibuprofen so 400 twice a day that helps some good have you hurt this ankle before not this one I sprained my left one in eighth grade but it healed fine no problem since any medicines you take every day or any allergies. Just saidy -razine, 10 milligrams in the spring for my allergies, I'm not on it right now. And I'm allergic to bactrim. I got a rash all over from it.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Got it, sulfa allergy with a rash.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Okay, let's take a look. Your blood pressure is 118 over 72, pulse 70.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: On your right ankle, there's swelling and some bruising on the outside, and your tender right here, in front of the ankle bone on the outside.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yeah, that's the spot.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: No tenderness on the back edge or tip of either ankle bone, and none at the base of your fifth toe bone or on top of the midfoot. When I pull your foot forward, it's a little loose compared to the left, but there's a firm end point. Pulses and feeling in your foot are normal. Can you walk across the room for me?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Sure, it's limpy, but okay. You took more than four steps on your own, good. So this is a sprain of the ligaments on the outside of your right ankle, probably grade 1 to 2.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Based on the exam,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: you meet the rules where we don't need an x -ray.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Oh, nice.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: My friend Diego tore his ACL last month, so my mom kind of freaked out.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Totally understandable,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: but your knee is fine.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Here's the plan.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Ice for 15 to 20 minutes every 2 to 3 hours for the next 2 days,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: keep it up on a pillow,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: and wear a compression wrap. We'll fit you with a lace -up ankle brace and wear it for practice for the next couple of months.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Keep the ibuprofen at 400 milligrams,

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: but every eight hours with food, for five to seven days, then just as needed. You can use crutches for two or three days if walking hurts, but put weight on it as much as you can. And start ankle alphabets, tracing the letters with your toes,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: a few times a day. When can I play again?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: We've got a tournament in November.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: No basketball for about two weeks. You can go back once you can hop and run on it without pain. I'll write a note for Coach Brennan and for gym class at Westfield High School. If you can't put weight on it, or the pain moves onto the bone, call us and we'll get an x -ray. If it's not much better in two weeks, come back and we'll set up physical therapy.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Cool. Can you send the note to my portal? My email is kenji .watneb11 at example .com. Sure,

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: and the phone number for you is 555 -0192.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yeah, that's my mom's cell.

turns.speaker: clinician
turns.text: Perfect. Nice sneakers, by the way. Thanks.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: They were a birthday present. Wrong ones to roll an ankle in, I guess.
